input.prompt:
Image 1 shows the real Spraymax bottle: a low-light photo of its front, and close-ups of its pump from the side and from the front. Use Image 1 only for the bottle's shape, proportions, plastic, ribbed collar, pump head, nozzle and clear overcap. Image 2 is the bottle's complete flat label artwork. Use Image 2 only for the label print, wrapped once around the body: its centre panel, with the indigo Spraymax wordmark running top to bottom, the line Instant Hair Volume & Texture and the dark navy ocean-wave band, faces the front, and the small-text panels wrap round the sides and back. Define the bottle from Image 1 wearing the label from Image 2 as <Subject 1>. <Subject 1> is identical in every shot.

Product truth: <Subject 1> is a slim 100 ml bottle about 14 cm tall, about four times as tall as it is wide, with a rounded shoulder, made of milky, slightly grey-white semi-matte plastic with a soft sheen and fine real surface texture; a matte white, finely ribbed collar; a small matte white pump head with a tiny round nozzle hole in its side, on the back-label side, so it is hidden whenever the front label faces the camera; a clear, lightly frosted overcap. The pump is a fine-mist sprayer: it releases only a soft cone of airborne droplets.

A 12-second vertical luxury campaign film for Spraymax Himalayan sea salt hair spray, cut like a high-end fragrance film: fifteen hard-cut shots of the bottle, its ingredients (Himalayan salt, sea water, aloe vera) and its fine mist, in cold blue light, each with one slow, deliberate camera move.

Hard cuts only throughout: every shot is a completely separate camera setup. No transitions, no dissolves, no wipes, no fades, no morphing, no motion carrying across a cut.

Real photography, inherited by every shot: filmed on an ARRI Alexa 35 with a 100 mm macro and an 85 mm cinema lens, the slow-motion shots on a Phantom high-speed camera at 1000 frames per second, with real practical effects (a fog machine for the smoke, a real water splash, real salt, a real aloe plant, real hands). Materials behave exactly as in life: water refracts and beads, salt is crystalline and slightly translucent, smoke is soft and uneven, skin shows pores and fine lines. Neutral white balance, deep clean blacks, natural film grain, gentle lens falloff and shallow focus; no beauty smoothing, no plastic sheen, no over-sharpening, no haze over the whole frame.

Global look: deep low-key, one hard light source per shot, roughly eighty percent black negative space, vertical 9:16. Cold light only, icy blue and silver-white with deep ocean-blue washes; the pink Himalayan salt is the only warm-toned element, and skin keeps its natural tone. Light is soft and unfocused where it blooms and hard and raking where it strikes. Framing alternates deliberately between extreme macro, where the bottle is cropped and only partly readable, and wide, where it stands small in a large black field.

Never render: a glossy or mirrored studio floor; a reflection of the bottle on a studio surface; a visible light fixture of any kind, including neon tubes, LED rings, hoops, strips, lamps or softboxes; a glowing halo directly behind the product; lens flares; liquid pouring, dripping or streaming from the nozzle; a warped, bent, melting or resized bottle; misspelled, mirrored or duplicated label text; extra or missing fingers; any face, or any person other than the first-person hands in the shot at 00:08.1; any text other than the bottle's own label; captions or watermarks; purple or violet light; the bottle centred and fully lit in every shot.

[00:00.0] Extreme close-up of the matte white ribbed collar and pump head of <Subject 1>, overcap removed, filling the frame against pure black. Camera pushes in slowly on a motion-control slider while a hard cool white key travels across the collar, catching the ribs one by one, the far side staying in near-total shadow.

[00:01.2] Extreme macro of two raw chunks of pale pink Himalayan rock salt touching, frosted cleaved facets and fine white veins, a fine sea-water mist drifting across them and settling as tiny beads, against a deep blue backdrop. Camera drifts slowly to the right.

[00:01.8] A real aloe vera plant seen straight from above, its thick, pointed, serrated leaves fanning out from the centre in a rosette, cold rim light catching the leaf edges and the pale speckles, everything else falling into black. Camera drifts laterally to the right.

[00:02.4] Medium macro, symmetrical and centred. The ribbed collar and pump head of <Subject 1> rise slowly up through the open centre of the aloe rosette, its leaves fanning either side, a cold backlight coming up behind them. Camera pushes in slowly.

[00:03.0] A slow curl of silvery-blue stage smoke rolling and unfurling in black space, soft, uneven and translucent, lit from one side by a cold key, nothing else in frame. Camera drifts to the right through it.

[00:03.7] <Subject 1> with its overcap on stands in a black void, front label to camera, a broad unfocused wash of deep ocean-blue light blooming behind it from an unseen source, the milky plastic taking a cool gradient from top to bottom. Camera pushes in slowly as the wash rises.

[00:04.8] Macro on the base of the front label of <Subject 1>: the dark ocean-wave photo band and the words FOR ALL HAIR TYPES fill the frame, printed exactly as in Image 2, the label edge crisp, a cold light grazing across the print. Camera pushes in slowly.

[00:05.6] Extreme macro, camera locked still. A single bead of sea water slides diagonally down the upper body of <Subject 1>, leaving a thin wet trail on the milky plastic, backlit ice blue so the water glows against it.

[00:06.2] Abstract macro. The camera tracks right, fast, across the ribbed collar of <Subject 1> on a slider, the ribs streaking past as vertical bands of black and burning blue-white with natural motion blur, the product unreadable.

[00:06.8] Low three-quarter view of <Subject 1> with its overcap on in near-silhouette against black, one thin silver highlight running down its edge and nothing else lit. Camera creeps in and rises toward the collar.

[00:07.4] Five identical bottles, each exactly <Subject 1> with its overcap on and its front label to camera, standing shoulder to shoulder in a straight row, cold blue-white light burning through the narrow gaps between them from behind, the bottles almost in silhouette. Camera drifts laterally to the left.

[00:08.1] First-person view, real hands only. One hand holds <Subject 1> upright with the overcap off; the index finger presses the pump once and a fine cone of mist leaves the nozzle hole in the side of the pump head and drifts sideways onto the open palm of the other hand, settling as tiny glinting droplets. Natural skin, cold light from above. The camera holds its distance, gently handheld.

[00:08.8] Phantom slow motion, locked-off camera. <Subject 1> with its overcap on stands in a shallow tray of dark sea water; a stream of water poured from above strikes the surface beside it and the water erupts into a crown splash round its base, droplets flying outward and catching a cold blue backlight.

[00:09.4] Phantom slow motion, macro side view of the pump head of <Subject 1>, overcap removed, camera locked still. A fine cone of mist bursts sideways out of the nozzle hole, backlit ice blue so every droplet catches the light, tight at the nozzle and blooming wide and translucent before thinning into black.

[00:10.0] Wide packshot. <Subject 1> with its overcap on stands left of centre on a deep ocean-blue matte surface, front label to camera, a long hard grounding shadow raking away to the right, the upper half of the frame left in empty darkness. Camera pushes in very slowly, almost imperceptibly.

Throughout: <Subject 1> keeps its exact shape, size, label and colours from Images 1 and 2, the label sharp and correctly spelled; no new reflections. Keep it subtitle-free, with no captions and no watermark. No other logos. No music and no voices.
